names_in_chart.icons: neutral monograms (white first letter on a coloured squircle); no category glyphs
names_in_chart.row_order: A–Z, stated on the page by a 'Sort: A–Z' / 'Sırala: A–Z' chip
names_in_chart.position_note: Extremes (Gisano/Libezu) sit in rows 2 and 4; top and bottom rows are mid-usage apps. In the q3 pair the visually larger app (Kuvelo) is the lower row, so a residual 'higher row = more' habit points to the text answer on q3a/q3b and to the visual answer on q1/q2 (row 2 vs row 4): 2 questions each way.
names_in_chart.names_note: coined names, identical in en/tr, no English/Turkish meaning or category root. Row 4 was 'Rimso' in an earlier version; RIMSO is a registered mark (RIMSO-50, a DMSO drug), so it was replaced by 'Libezu'. Search 2026-10-05 for the bare word 'libezu': Google Play search -> 'No results'; App Store (web search on apps.apple.com) -> no Libezu app (closest 'Libanezu', a different word); USPTO via Trademarkia -> 0 results (Justia returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches); general web -> no exact match.
names_in_chart.design_deviation: DESIGN.md plan: Chirp/Tubeo/Mapster/Notely/Bankly sorted longest first, q3 Chirp vs Tubeo, q4 Tubeo (visual 7h 10m, text 2h 30m). Built: coined names in A–Z rows with a sort chip, q3 Dorvi vs Kuvelo, q4 Dorvi (visual 2h 30m, text 7h 10m), so names and row position carry no cue (see make.py docstring).
names_in_chart.read_value_note: q4 conflict: the visual answer 2h 30m is printed in the image, on Kuvelo's row, 2 rows below Dorvi. Bars have no scale, so geometry alone cannot give that exact value: a 'visual' hit means a value reached by rank re-mapping or a misread row, not a bar measurement.
names_in_chart.nonumbers_note: per-app time labels blanked (span kept at its fixed width, holding one no-break space); weekly total and daily average kept (identical in all versions). q1-q3 answerable from bar lengths; q4 not (bars have no scale).

prompt: answer tr tlwy son bir ayda yükseldi mi düştü mü?
chart: finance app watchlist (light web app) · sparklines

names_in_chart.third_cue_guard: largest |change| = TLWY (text winner), so 'pick the biggest number' fails the consistent control; highest/lowest last price = KDNL / VESK (neither winner)
names_in_chart.no_read_value: No 'what was X's 1-month change' question: there is no y-axis, so in conflict the magnitude can only come from the printed text, and a sign-dropped or sign-in-words reading of that text ('12.7%', 'minus 12.7', 'eksi 12,7') would score as a geometry win. A sign-read check would need a separate, unpooled control row type in common/collect.py + the notebook.
names_in_chart.analysis_note: q1 has a magnitude confound: in conflict the text winner TLWY is also the line with the biggest move and shaded area, so a direction-blind 'most dramatic line' pick scores as text (the consistent control removes only readers who do this every time). Weight q2, q3a/q3b and q4a/q4b, which have no magnitude confound, above q1 when concluding 'text wins'.
